anomalies.observed: On the CAN Bus sheet, the two 8-pin circular connectors 'J11 CAN Interface A' and 'J37 CAN Interface B' both carry the identical nets on pins 2-5 (NET0118, NET0165, NET0017, NET0036), while only pin 1 differs between the two connectors (NET0034 on J11 vs NET0024 on J37). The four differential/channel signals therefore appear on both connectors.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes two independent isolated CAN buses: 'two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion), broken out on M12 circular connectors J2 ("CAN Interface A") and J13 ("CAN Interface B")'. The CAN_H/CAN_L pair of Interface A and of Interface B must be separate nets, so the two channels are not shorted together at the connectors.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion), broken out on M12 circular connectors J2 ("CAN Interface A") and J13 ("CAN Interface B")
CAN Bus sheet: J11 'CAN Interface A' pins 2-5 labeled NET0118, NET0165, NET0017, NET0036; J37 'CAN Interface B' pins 2-5 labeled NET0118, NET0165, NET0017, NET0036

anomalies.impact: If the two CAN channels share these connections, the isolation between CAN interface A and CAN interface B is defeated at the connectors: traffic on one channel appears on the other, the two buses cannot be used independently, and the four ODrive controllers could not be addressed on separate buses as intended.

parsed.summary: The design largely matches the specification, but on the CAN Bus sheet the two circular 'CAN Interface A' (J11) and 'CAN Interface B' (J37) connectors appear to carry the same four signal nets on pins 2-5, which would short the two isolated CAN channels that the specification says must be separate; this is the main candidate anomaly found.
